cases.answer:
The two unsupervised tasks used to pre-train BERT are:

- Masked Language Modeling (MLM), where some percentage of the input tokens are randomly masked and the model is trained to predict these masked tokens [1][3].
- Next Sentence Prediction (NSP), where the model is trained to predict whether one sentence follows another in the original text, by labeling pairs as either IsNext (the second sentence is the actual next sentence) or NotNext (the second sentence is a random sentence from the corpus) [1][3].

additional_claims.claim: MLM masks input tokens and predicts them.
NSP distinguishes the actual next sentence from a random sentence.

cases.review: Cited page-4 prose defines MLM masking/prediction and NSP actual-next versus random sentences. Both added explanations are supported; no diagram is needed.
